_meta.title: Round 2 market research (MochaTrade Track 1)

evidence_tags.[V]: verified against a primary source (regulator, FATF, statute)
evidence_tags.[V-secondary]: verified via a law-firm, news or other secondary source
evidence_tags.[V-draft]: verified, but the rule is a draft / not in force
evidence_tags.[A]: assumption or limited evidence -- confirm before relying on it
evidence_tags.[D]: derived by the researcher from the facts cited

_meta.scoring: Scores use the Round 1 rubric (25/25/20/15/15). 'screening_score_sheet' is the workbook's printed total; the engine recomputes it and a test checks they agree.
_meta.clearing: A market clears at base weights when score >= the 3.0 threshold AND it passes the regulatory knock-out (legality > 2 and licence > 1). Computed by the engine, not stored.
_meta.sequencing: Round 2 markets are NOT sequenced: the workbook has no entry route, timing window or go-gates. Cleared ones get the 'shortlist' verdict; researched adaptation / execution are shown and used only for an indicative priority comparison against the Round 1 plan.
_meta.round1_notes: Round 1 markets keep their deck scores and text verbatim. Research notes and 'deck_check' refinements are shown alongside, never substituted.

philippines.adaptation_rationale: [D] No evidence of a licensed retail-perpetuals route; likely spot/structured or local-exchange product; local office + local data centre required.
philippines.execution_rationale: [D] BSP VASP licences frozen (moratorium indefinite since 2025); SEC CASP route needs a Philippine entity -> partner-led via a licensed VASP/bank is the practical route.
philippines.payment_rail: InstaPay/PESONet (PCHC), GCash/Maya wallets [A - LIMITED EVIDENCE]. Access only via BSP-supervised banks/EMIs. BSP draft (7 Sep 2026) would freeze new payment-operator applications for 12 months and treat VASPs as 'high-risk merchants' [V - draft, news-reported].
philippines.capital_and_licensing: SEC MC No.4 & 5 (30 May 2025): PHP100M paid-up (~US$1.7M at ~PHP58/USD, [D]); PHP50k filing fee; physical office; data centre; client-asset segregation [V-secondary]. BSP VASP moratorium on new licences [V-secondary]; 5 licensed VASPs stay authorised. Standalone possible only via SEC route + local entity.
philippines.kyc_aml: BSP Circular 1108 travel rule above PHP50,000 [V-secondary]. Not on FATF grey list (Jun 2026) [V]. PhilSys ID [A].
philippines.product_changes: No retail leverage cap or derivatives permission found [A]; SEC CASP rules silent on derivatives. Unlicensed foreign platforms blocked (SEC advisory Aug 2025: OKX, Bybit, KuCoin etc.). US equities: SEC broker/dealer licence likely [A].
philippines.regulatory_basis: SEC MC 04/05-2025; BSP Circular 1108; BSP moratorium release; BSP 7 Sep 2026 draft
philippines.deck_check: Consistent with deck. Refinement: BSP moratorium is indefinite (start date varies Sep 2022/Aug-Sep 2025 by source); the 7 Sep 2026 BSP item is a separate payments draft.

nigeria.adaptation_rationale: [D] Draft is silent on derivatives/margin/leverage; retail caps + suitability apply; perpetuals would need explicit SEC approval.
nigeria.execution_rationale: [D] Local entity + Nigeria-resident CEO (unless exempted); rules still draft -> local partner advisable.
nigeria.payment_rail: NIP (NIBSS) / bank transfer [A - LIMITED EVIDENCE]; open to banks and licensed PSPs only, so a foreign operator needs a licensed partner.
nigeria.capital_and_licensing: SEC draft 'Digital and Virtual Assets Operations, Custody and Markets' rules (published 20 Aug 2026; comments closed 3 Sep 2026; NOT in force) [V-secondary]: exchanges/custodians NGN2bn (~US$1.5M), platform operators NGN500M, VASPs NGN200M; registration NGN30M (VASP NGN15M); fidelity bond >=25% of capital. Basis: Investments & Securities Act 2025 (digital assets = securities). Draft SEC cross-border trading rules (2 Jul 2026): NGN2bn net liquid capital, SEC 'no objection', IOSCO-member foreign brokers [V-draft]. Virtual Assets Coordination Executive Order signed 17 Jul 2026 [V-secondary]. Final SEC rules not found.
nigeria.kyc_aml: Not on FATF grey list [V]. NIN/BVN/TIN ID basis [A]; travel-rule text not found.
nigeria.product_changes: Perpetuals neither permitted nor banned in draft; no leverage cap found [A]. Retail limits NGN1M per issuer / NGN10M per year for offering platforms; suitability + consent flows. US equities: only via SEC-registered brokers under draft cross-border rules (0.35% SEC fee on foreign purchases).
nigeria.deck_check: Consistent with deck. Refinement: NGN2bn applies to exchanges/custodians; VASP tier is NGN200M. Comment window has closed - check for final text.

pakistan.adaptation_rationale: [D] A 'derivatives' licence class exists, so perpetuals have an explicit category (unique among the three); leverage terms unknown; needs Pakistani company and rupee banking.
pakistan.execution_rationale: [D] Pakistan-incorporated company, NOC route, bank partners for client-money accounts, brand-new untested regime.
pakistan.payment_rail: Raast (SBP) likely [A - LIMITED EVIDENCE]. SBP Circular 10 of 2026 (15 Apr 2026) lets banks open accounts incl. client-money accounts for PVARA-licensed VASPs [V-secondary]; unlicensed foreign operators cannot use them.
pakistan.capital_and_licensing: Virtual Assets Act 2026 (Act XIII, enacted 4 Mar 2026) created PVARA [V-secondary]. Min paid-up capital: derivatives PKR500M (~US$1.8M at ~PKR280/USD, [D]), exchange PKR500M, custody PKR200M, broker-dealer PKR75M; liquidity floor 1.2x monthly opex [V-secondary, law-firm]. Track B (NOC) needs Pakistan-registered company; Track A sandbox. Transitional-operator NOC deadline 5 Sep 2026 has passed. Fees/timeline not published.
pakistan.kyc_aml: Act requires CDD, transaction monitoring, SAR filing, sanctions screening [V-secondary]. Not on FATF grey list [V]. CNIC/NADRA, travel rule, FMU reporting [A].
pakistan.product_changes: No leverage cap or retail restriction found; PVARA Virtual Asset Services Regulations 2026 consultation not read [A]. Tokenised/US stocks: SBP outward-remittance limits are the barrier; not regulated by SECP/PSX per local sources [A].
pakistan.deck_check: Deck says 'licensing opened Aug 2026'; framework actually began Mar-Apr 2026 (Act, SBP Circular 10) with NOC portal ~Aug 2026. 'Rupee-only accounts' not found in sources reviewed - confirm before citing. Deck could add derivatives licence class + PKR500M.

thailand.adaptation_rationale: [D] Retail access only to foreign products that mirror Thai-permitted derivatives (underlying, leverage, maturity, settlement, CCP-cleared); non-CCP crypto perpetuals likely do not qualify; non-conforming products institutional-only.
thailand.execution_rationale: [D] Access only via licensed Thai intermediaries; foreign app cannot offer directly; final rules not issued.
thailand.payment_rail: PromptPay (BOT) / Thai bank transfers [A - LIMITED EVIDENCE]; in practice via licensed Thai bank/e-wallet partner.
thailand.capital_and_licensing: SEC digital-asset licences need a Thai limited/public company: exchange THB50M (~US$1.5M at ~THB33/USD, [D]), broker/dealer THB25M, DEX THB10M [V-secondary]. Derivatives-licence capital and foreign-ownership limits NOT found. SEC proposal announced 31 Aug 2026, consultation closes 30 Sep 2026, no implementation date [V-news]; SEC recognised crypto as derivatives underlying Mar 2026.
thailand.kyc_aml: Not on FATF grey list [V]. Thai ID/AMLO reporting/travel rule [A - not verified].
thailand.product_changes: Perpetual eligibility depends on final rules; no leverage cap published (tied to TFEX specs) [A]. Does not legalise direct use of offshore exchanges. US equities: via Thai licensed brokers; foreign platform would need Thai licence [A].
thailand.deck_check: Consistent with deck ('proposal only'); consultation closes 30 Sep 2026 - recheck outcome.

south_africa.adaptation_rationale: [D] Perpetuals already licensable (VALR ODP licence, 20 Oct 2025 covers perpetual futures, CFDs); changes = FSCA licensing, retail disclosures, exchange-control compliance.
south_africa.execution_rationale: [D] FSCA FSP/ODP licence via local entity or licensed partner; long timeline (vendor estimate 12-24 months [A]).
south_africa.payment_rail: EFT/instant EFT, PayShap (PayInc) [A - LIMITED EVIDENCE]; bank/PSP participant access; SARB payment reforms still draft.
south_africa.capital_and_licensing: Crypto = financial product (FSCA Notice 1350, 19 Oct 2022); CASP regime since 1 Jun 2023; crypto derivatives are securities under Financial Markets Act -> FSP + ODP licence needed, not just CASP [V-secondary]. ODP: 6 months' opex at all times; advisory estimate ZAR5-15M+ (~US$275-825k) is a vendor estimate, not regulation [A]. Local (Pty) entity, 2 experienced directors.
south_africa.kyc_aml: FICA; FIC travel-rule directive applies to all CASPs [V-secondary]. Exited FATF grey list 24 Oct 2025 [V]. SA ID/FICA documents [A].
south_africa.product_changes: Retail leverage cap not found [A]. Draft Capital Flow Management Regulations (gazetted 17 Apr 2026; comments to 30 Jun 2026; NOT final): crypto transfers above thresholds must go via Treasury-authorised CASP; penalties up to R1m/5 yrs [V-draft]. US equities: FSP licence + exchange-control offshore allowances [A].
south_africa.deck_check: Deck says '310 CASPs licensed'; best source found says ~300 approved of 512 applications (FSCA, Jan 2026) - verify 310. Draft CFM rule routes flows via authorised CASPs rather than banning self-custody outright - deck wording ('blocks self-custody transfers') is somewhat strong.

vietnam.adaptation_rationale: [D] VND-only settlement, stablecoins banned, spot-only pilot, INR/UPI funding model cannot work; no evidence derivatives permitted.
vietnam.execution_rationale: [D] Foreign holding capped at 49%; >=65% Vietnamese institutions; ~5 licences for whole pilot; none issued.
vietnam.payment_rail: NAPAS 247 / VietQR bank-centred [A - LIMITED EVIDENCE]; SBV bars financial institutions from crypto payments [V-secondary].
vietnam.capital_and_licensing: Resolution 05/2025/NQ-CP (Sep 2025, 5-year pilot): min charter capital VND10 trillion (~US$380M [D]); foreign cap 49%; VND settlement only [V-secondary]. Applications opened 20 Jan 2026 (MoF Decision 96/QD-BTC). As of Sep 2026: 7 applicants, 5 passed initial assessment, NO licence issued [V-news]. Penalty decree for unlicensed operations 1 Sep 2026. Standalone impossible for a foreign firm; minority JV only [D].
vietnam.kyc_aml: Identity checks, monitoring, reporting [V-secondary]; CCCD/VNeID [A]. Vietnam is on FATF grey list (Jun 2026 page) [V].
vietnam.product_changes: Spot crypto only within pilot; no permission for perpetuals/derivatives or US-equity routes found [A].
vietnam.deck_check: Consistent with deck; adds >=65% Vietnamese-institution requirement, no licences issued and FATF grey-list status.

deep_dive.crypto_route: Register as a DASP under the Digital Assets Issuance Law (in force 1 Feb 2024) with CNAD. Exchange/platform activity is permitted; derivatives and leverage require CNAD counsel confirmation before launch.
deep_dive.equities_route: No US-equities route found; not researched.

deep_dive.kyc_aml: KYC/KYT required; US$1,000 transaction limit mentioned in Aug 2024 reform proposal (unconfirmed). Not on FATF grey list.
deep_dive.capital_and_licensing: CNAD DASP registration under Digital Assets Issuance Law; one-time fee US$5,475; ≤20 business days; minimum capital reported ~US$2,000 by one secondary source (low confidence). Standalone, local-entity registration.
deep_dive.commercial_adoption: Dollarised economy — no FX friction. Chivo wallet adoption is high but Bitcoin usage remains limited; retail demand for US-equity and perps products is unverified.

research.payment_rail: Fawri+/Benefit [A]; likely via Bahraini licensed entity/bank.

Cat 1-3 need Bahrain place of business and resident controlled functions. Standalone but local office. Own-account positions capped at 50% of paid-up capital [V].

research.product_changes: Derivatives 'require separate CBB approval' with derivatives risk framework [V]; no leverage cap found [A]. US equities via separate CBB investment-firm route [A].

deep_dive.qualifies_reason: CBB Crypto-Asset Module (Rulebook Vol.6 CRA) is the most established Gulf VASP regime outside the UAE. Cat 3 (~US$530k) or Cat 4 (~US$795k) exchange licence. Derivatives require a separate CBB approval with a derivatives risk framework.
deep_dive.crypto_route: CBB Cat 3 or Cat 4 licence under Crypto-Asset Module (CRA) in CBB Rulebook Vol.6. Derivatives require separate CBB approval with a derivatives risk framework — this is a second licensing track.
deep_dive.equities_route: Separate CBB investment-firm route; not researched.
deep_dive.required_product_changes: Apply for CBB CRA Cat 3 or 4 licence; submit derivatives risk framework for separate CBB approval; establish Bahrain place of business with resident controlled functions; connect to Fawri+/Benefit via a Bahraini licensed entity or bank; implement AML/CFT to CBB standards
deep_dive.kyc_aml: Robust CBB AML/CFT requirements; travel-rule wording not seen in source. Not on FATF grey list.
deep_dive.capital_and_licensing: CBB CRA Rulebook Vol.6: Cat 1 BD25k, Cat 2 BD100k, Cat 3 BD200k (~US$530k), Cat 4 BD300k (~US$795k — exchange). Bahrain place of business and resident controlled functions required. CBB 2022 Rulebook version — 2025–26 amendments known only via secondary sources.
deep_dive.commercial_adoption: Small but wealthy market (~1.5M pop.); established Gulf financial hub; strong regulatory clarity is the differentiator from the wider region.
deep_dive.local_payment_rail: Fawri+/Benefit — likely via a Bahraini licensed entity or bank (assumption)

deep_dive.commercial_adoption: ~6M crypto holders (~16% population) despite the ban; highest crypto transaction value in North Africa (2023); significant pent-up demand. Market unlocks only on enactment.
deep_dive.local_payment_rail: Moroccan bank transfers (dirham) — foreign operator cannot access rails while the 2017 ban is in force
deep_dive.main_hurdle: Bill 42.25 must be enacted and the 2017 joint ban formally withdrawn before any operation is lawful

deep_dive.qualifies_reason: Do not enter: all crypto transactions are treated as contraventions of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947; Bangladesh Bank reaffirmed the ban as recently as Sep 2025 and threatened licence revocation for facilitators. No exceptions.
deep_dive.crypto_route: Bangladesh Bank has declared all crypto transactions in violation of the FER Act 1947, Money Laundering Prevention Act 2012 and Anti-Terrorism Act 2009. Warning Notice BB/CC/2025/17 (Sep 2025) threatened licence revocation and criminal prosecution for any entity facilitating crypto. No licensing authority or category exists.
deep_dive.equities_route: Not researched. Outward remittances under FER Act require authorisation; US equities route not viable under current rules.
deep_dive.required_product_changes: Do not operate or target Bangladeshi users. Monitor Bangladesh Bank for any policy reversal; no actionable steps are possible while the FER Act ban is in force.
deep_dive.kyc_aml: Comprehensive AML framework (Money Laundering Prevention Act 2012; Anti-Terrorism Act 2009) — but crypto is outside the regulated financial system and bank accounts associated with crypto are instructed to be closed.
deep_dive.capital_and_licensing: No licensing authority or category exists. Bangladesh Bank has stated it will not relax the ban until its regulatory infrastructure is stronger.
deep_dive.commercial_adoption: 170M+ population; large remittance market. Crypto activity is underground and illegal. Market is closed until Bangladesh Bank withdraws the FER Act position.
deep_dive.local_payment_rail: bKash/Nagad and bank transfers — crypto platforms cannot access these rails; banks are instructed to close associated accounts
deep_dive.main_hurdle: Bangladesh Bank must withdraw the FER Act prohibition; no actionable steps possible until then

research.reserve_reason: Law 194/2020 prohibits crypto without CBE licence; none granted.

deep_dive.qualifies_reason: Do not enter: Article 206 of Law 194/2020 prohibits all crypto trading and platform operation without CBE approval; no licence has ever been issued; penalties include imprisonment and fines up to EGP10M.
deep_dive.crypto_route: Article 206 of Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194/2020 prohibits issuing, trading, promoting or operating a crypto platform without prior CBE approval. No approval procedure has been published; no licence has ever been issued. CBE issued a fourth public warning in 2025.
deep_dive.required_product_changes: Do not operate or target Egyptian users. Monitor CBE for any published licensing procedure. No actionable steps are possible while Article 206 is enforced without a licence procedure.
deep_dive.kyc_aml: General AML obligations apply to licensed financial institutions; no bespoke crypto AML/CFT framework because crypto is outside the regulated system. Dar al-Ifta 2018 fatwa (non-binding) declared crypto haram.
deep_dive.capital_and_licensing: No licence procedure published. Article 206 theoretically permits CBE to grant approval, but as of 2026 no procedure, no fee, no capital requirement and no timeline exist.
deep_dive.commercial_adoption: ~3M holders via offshore/P2P channels despite the ban. CBE framing is consumer protection and capital-flight prevention. Market unlocks only if CBE publishes a licence procedure.
deep_dive.local_payment_rail: Meeza/IBANS instant payment — crypto platforms are outside the regulated system and cannot access rails
deep_dive.main_hurdle: CBE must publish a licensing procedure under Article 206 before any operation is lawful; none exists as of 2026
